title: Introduce intake contract lifecycle and performance encapsulation
author: Maria Valdez
description:
Motivation: onboarding flux has shown two recurring problems: (1) metadata drift between intake manifests and final profiles, which makes release notes noisy; and (2) missing per-variant performance footprints, which prevents accurate capacity planning and rollout gating. This PR introduces a first-class intake contract lifecycle and a compact performance encapsulation artifact attached to each model/variant.

What this changes: added a lifecycle state machine for intake contracts (draft -> validated -> approved -> staged -> stable -> retired) with an explicit transition API and audit hooks; a lightweight 'perf-encap' blob format (JSON LZ4 compressed) that stores canonical median/p90 latency, sample token throughput, memory footprint hints, and test harness pointers; migration tooling to backfill perf-encap for previously onboarded models using sampled telemetry and eval-harness replays; and a compatibility check that verifies model artifact signatures and schema compatibility before transitions to approved/stable.

Files & surface area: new API endpoints in registry service: POST /intake/contracts, PATCH /intake/contracts/:id/transition, GET /intake/contracts/:id/perf-encap; registry DB schema changes (contracts table, perf_encap column blob ref); onboarding CLI additions (redwood-modelctl contract validate/emit-encap); a lightweight backfill job (bin/rmr-backfill-perf-encap) that runs under the telemetry migration pipeline.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged at registry.feature.intake_lifecycle; initial rollout will run in read-only validation mode for two weeks to collect failures; then allow write transitions for internal models; after one month we will enable for all incoming models. Backfill job is opt-in and gated by linear ticket ENG-1423.

Migration notes: a migration script migrates the existing "profile" records to include a perf-encap pointer; temporary compatibility layer ensures old clients can still read profiles (profiles include a legacy_perf_summary field until 2026-02-01). Backfill includes a confidence score; low-confidence encap entries are marked as 'probe' and excluded from autoscaling decisions until validated.

Testing and observability: end-to-end tests added in registry-integration and eval-harness integration suite. New metrics: rmr.contract.transition.count, rmr.perf_encap.generated.count, rmr.perf_encap.backfill.duration_ms; added a Dashboard tile in Console (Model Registry -> Contracts) showing lifecycle distribution and average footprint by model family.

Security and compliance: perf-encap blobs respect PII rules (no prompts or sample outputs captured). Signing of artifacts relies on existing artifact-signer service; the compatibility check validates signatures.

Future work: (1) wire perf-encap into routing heuristics in serving runtime for auto-variant-selection, (2) integrate perf-encap into Redwood Optimize recommendations, (3) refine compression format if we need lower latency access.

Related tickets: ENG-1423 (intake lifecycle), PM-305 (release footprint), SUP-87 (customer ask re: model rollout stability).

review_thread: Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid storing uncompressed JSON blobs in Postgres? Suggest storing S3 pointer + local cache policy.
Maria Valdez: Agree; perf_encap is an object store pointer. The serializer writes LZ4 to object store and stores pointer. Updated migration to reflect this.
Nadia Singh: Are there privacy risks from eval-harness replays? Please confirm prompts are not captured.
Maria Valdez: Confirmed, we only capture performance metrics and pointers to harness commits; no prompts or outputs are stored. Added explicit tests.
Ethan Zhao: LGTM but please add metric for backfill success ratio and a circuit breaker when memory footprint estimate is missing.
Maria Valdez: Added rmr.perf_encap.backfill.success_ratio and removal of encap from autoscaling path if memory estimate is absent.
release_notes: Adds an intake contract lifecycle with explicit state transitions, a compact performance encapsulation artifact for models, migration tooling and a backfill job. Enables better capacity planning and clearer release footprints. Opt-in backfill and feature-flagged rollout.
